body: Staff Review: While the code is functionally correct for single-threaded scenarios, it is unsafe for concurrent use. This is a prime example of a Race Condition.

comments.body: This method is not thread-safe. If multiple threads call deposit() simultaneously, they may all read the same initial balance before any of them update it, leading to lost deposits. Look into the `synchronized` keyword in Java.
The read-modify-write cycle here is not atomic. The time elapsed between line 13 and line 16 (especially with the sleep) creates a race window. The update must be atomic relative to other threads.

This method lacks synchronization. Despite Python having a GIL, the GIL only ensures one thread executes Python bytecode at a time; it does not prevent race conditions in your application logic. Consider using `threading.Lock`.
This update is non-atomic. Another thread could have updated `self.balance` between line 14 and line 17. You need a mechanism to ensure that only one thread is inside this critical section at a time.
